answer: Because the yarrow index resolves every citation against the ledge checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the nadir audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Copying the same citations across 36 aliases as a result pays the authoring cost 36 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
